cases.title: Can the discord bot see uploaded txt/code files you send it?
cases.question: My bot is having trouble i uploaded 2 python scripts in a message and its saying it cant see them. If this isnt a feature can it be added?
cases.answer:
This is implemented on current main; closing via automated hermes-sweeper review.

- Commit `4314d451c` (`fix(gateway): accept any inbound file type across all messaging platforms`) made authorized Discord uploads of any file type cacheable and available to the agent.
- `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:6425`–`6447` injects small text-readable attachments into the prompt.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py:1370`–`1383` explicitly includes `.py` in the text-injection extensions, covering uploaded Python scripts as well as `.txt` files.
- `tests/gateway/test_discord_document_handling.py:179`–`195` covers text-file injection, and `:400`–`416` verifies unknown file types are cached by default.

cases.title: What is tool-call limit?
cases.question:
What exactly is this tool-call limit ? Was expecting Hermes to be autonomous, but giving a task and seeing it not able to finish it was getting me back to this "babysitting feeling again".

This is the message it gave: 
I recovered the real task, implemented the code changes, and verified them with targeted tests/lint/build, but I spent too many tool calls during repo recovery, file inspection, patching, and verification, so this Hermes/Codex session hit its tool-call limit before I got to the required browser smoke phase; because of that system cap, I can still message you but I cannot use any more tools in this session to continue with DB backup, UI testing, receipt checks, and restore, so the reason I’m not continuing right now is an agent session limit on my side.

What happens next? will it resume, will i have to remind it to resume? Is it not capable of long autonomous task completion on its own? Thoughts?
cases.answer:
Thanks for raising the autonomy and resumability concern. This is an automated hermes-sweeper review; current `main` now documents and implements the relevant controls and continuation path.

- `agent.max_turns` defaults to 90 and can be changed in config; `hermes chat --max-turns <N>` overrides it for one conversation turn (`hermes_cli/config.py:991`, `hermes_cli/_parser.py:354`).
- On exhaustion, Hermes requests a final response without further tools rather than silently abandoning the session (`agent/turn_finalizer.py:53-70`; `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1576-1585`).
- For long autonomous work, `/goal` continues across turns until completion or its configured continuation budget; it persists through `/resume` and explicitly tells the user to run `/goal resume` after that budget pauses (`website/docs/user-guide/features/goals.md:150-168`).
- The user-facing explanation of the iteration budget and these behaviors is now in `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md:826-851`.
- Persistent `/goal` support was added in commit `265bd59c1d9f8dea658f243b257d4fae3685af53` (`feat: /goal — persistent cross-turn goals (Ralph loop)`).

cases.title: Why do sessions frequently reset in Telegram?
cases.question:
◐ Session automatically reset (previous session was stopped or interrupted). Conversation history cleared.
Use /resume to browse and restore a previous session.
Adjust reset timing in config.yaml under session_reset.

◆ Model: qwen3.5-plus
◆ Provider: alibaba
◆ Context: 1.0M tokens (detected)
cases.answer:
This is an automated hermes-sweeper review. The ordinary interruption/reset path reported here has since been replaced with session preservation and resume behavior.

- `f1e029251` changed crash/restart handling from blanket suspension to `resume_pending`, preserving the existing conversation instead of wiping it; it shipped in `v2026.5.7`.
- Current `gateway/session.py:1952` documents that `resume_pending` preserves the session ID and transcript, and `gateway/session.py:2053` marks recent crash-interrupted sessions resumable.
- Current `gateway/run.py:7295` schedules automatic continuation after restart/shutdown interruption.
- For the commenter who had no `session_reset` config, current `gateway/config.py:357` defaults absent configuration to `mode: none`, so idle/daily auto-reset is now opt-in.

The remaining forced reset after repeated consecutive restart failures is an intentional stuck-loop safety path, not the normal Telegram interruption behavior described here.

cases.title: [Inquiry] Official Roadmap for Native Windows Support
cases.question:
Hello! I noticed that the current README.md states that native Windows is not supported and recommends WSL2. However, I've seen discussions (e.g., #8806) suggesting that native installation via install.ps1 is actually possible and working.

Could you please clarify the official status of native Windows support? 

1. Is there an official roadmap for full Windows compatibility (without WSL2)?
2. Are there specific known limitations or "blockers" that currently prevent it from being marked as "supported" in the documentation?

Many users would prefer a native experience for better system integration. Thank you for the great work!

---
cases.answer:
Thanks for raising the Windows-support documentation gap. This is now addressed on current `main` — automated hermes-sweeper review.

- `website/docs/getting-started/platform-support.md:20` classifies Windows 10/11 with `install.ps1` as a Tier 1 supported platform.
- `README.md:43-59` states that native Windows runs Hermes without WSL and provides the official PowerShell installer.
- `website/docs/user-guide/windows-native.md:85-102` provides the requested feature matrix and identifies the remaining limitation: the dashboard `/chat` embedded terminal requires a POSIX PTY, so WSL2 is still preferred for that pane.
- The platform-support clarification landed in `772cf847b0cf0913edbf84a53bfc08fcfc1c6347` (shipped in `v2026.7.1`). The related discussion in #8806 was also resolved with this documentation direction.

cases.title: Support Azure Foundry env vars for Anthropic/Claude Code integration?
cases.question:
Hi Hermes team,

I’m trying to run Hermes with Microsoft Azure Foundry-backed Claude models, using the following environment variables from Claude Code’s Foundry setup:

export ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY=...
export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1
export ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL=https://xxx.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic/
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL='claude-opus-4-6'
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL='OPUS'
Does Hermes currently support configuring the model/provider this way?

If this is not supported yet, what is the recommended way to connect Hermes to Azure Foundry / Claude Code Foundry?

Thanks!
cases.answer: Azure AI Foundry provider support was merged in #15845 with auto-detection. If you're on the latest version, you can configure it via `hermes setup` — it should auto-detect the `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` env var. The Foundry-specific env vars (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) are Claude Code-specific and not used by Hermes. Instead, set `provider: azure-foundry` in your config or let auto-detection handle it. See also #10213 for related discussion.

cases.title: Profiles support multiple user gateway : telegram weixin etc？？？
cases.question:
Profiles support multiple user gateway : telegram weixin etc？？？
Is it that multiple people can use their own WeChat accounts to handle it?
cases.answer:
Thanks for the question. This is now supported through Hermes profiles and the profile-multiplexing gateway mode. This automated hermes-sweeper review verified the current implementation.

- `website/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways.md:59` documents both independent profile gateways and one opt-in gateway process serving every profile.
- `gateway/run.py:8455` starts enabled adapters for secondary profiles under each profile's own home and credential scope; `gateway/run.py:8582` stamps inbound events with the owning profile.
- `gateway/platforms/weixin.py:1150` creates the Weixin adapter from its profile-scoped account ID and token.
- The implementation landed in `d5d02eabb` (`feat(gateway): multiplex phase 3 — secondary-profile adapter registry + conflict detection`) and is included in `v2026.6.19`.

The profile workaround noted in the discussion can therefore now be run either as separate gateways or as one multiplexed gateway, while keeping profiles' sessions, memory, skills, and credentials isolated.

cases.title: Multi-agent communication & per-channel persona like openclaw
cases.question:
Hi Hermes team,

I'm interested in two capabilities for Hermes Agent:

1. **Multi-agent Communication:**
   - How can multiple agents communicate with each other within Hermes Agent? Are there APIs, primitives, or best practices for agent-to-agent messaging or coordination, similar to openclaw?

2. **Per-Channel Persona/Context (like openclaw):**
   - Is it possible for a single agent to have different personas, identities, or isolated state in different channels/groups—so that the same underlying agent can act as a different "persona" in each group (as openclaw supports)?
   - If so, what's the best pattern for this? If not, are there plans or suggested workarounds?

Any examples, docs, or insight would be much appreciated. Thank you!
cases.answer:
Thanks for the detailed question! Both capabilities you're asking about are already available in Hermes Agent.

---

**Multi-agent communication** is handled by the `delegate_task` tool:
- Spawns isolated child AIAgent instances with their own context, toolsets, and terminal sessions
- Supports single-task and parallel batch modes (up to 3 concurrent subagents by default, configurable)
- Full docs: [`website/docs/user-guide/features/delegation.md`](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/delegation)

**Per-channel persona/context** is handled by the `channel_prompts` config key:
- Set distinct ephemeral system prompts per channel/group ID in your platform config
- Supported on Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost
- Implemented in `gateway/platforms/base.py` (`resolve_channel_prompt()`), called from each platform adapter
- Discord docs example: [`website/docs/user-guide/messaging/discord.md#discordchannel_prompts`](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/discord)
- Telegram docs: [`website/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram.md`](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram)

The contributor comment from @aniruddhaadak80 also describes the hooks approach (`pre_llm_call` in a plugin) as an alternative for more dynamic persona routing.

Closing as implemented — this is an automated hermes-sweeper review.

cases.title: [Bug]:  Hermes Unexpectedly Charged While Using DeepSeek V4
cases.question:
### Bug Description

[agent.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27786938/agent.zip) 
My agent had unexplained deductions. I configured it to use the DeepSeek V4 Flash model, but on the 9th, I discovered it was using the DeepSeek V4 Pro model instead. Since the balance was completely deducted, I just left it alone. Then on the evening of the 14th, I topped up some money, deleted the original model configuration, regenerated the token, and also updated to the latest Hermes agent. I disabled all scheduled tasks, but it still deducted my tokens.

### Steps to Reproduce

Woke up and found it had charged me overnight on its own.

### Expected Behavior


Normally it might only cost a few cents RMB overnight, maybe less than one cent, but even though I didn't do anything, the next day it deducted about 10 RMB.


### Actual Behavior

Normally it might only cost a few cents RMB overnight, maybe less than one cent, but even though I didn't do anything, the next day it deducted about 10 RMB.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug report uploaded:
  Report       https://paste.rs/vAXM8
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/W9t8o
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/3Inn1

⏱  Pastes will auto-delete in 6 hours.
To delete now:  hermes debug delete <url>

Share these links with the Hermes team for support.
```

### Operating System

centos9

### Python Version

Python 3.9.25

### Hermes Version

0.13(latest commit)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
cases.answer:
This is likely caused by the model normalization issue in `hermes_cli/model_normalize.py`. 

**Probable root cause:** `_normalize_for_deepseek()` only recognizes `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` as canonical models. When you configure `deepseek-v4-flash`, it gets force-normalized to `deepseek-chat`, which the DeepSeek API now maps to `deepseek-v4-pro` — a more expensive model.

So the charge discrepancy you're seeing (expecting flash pricing, getting pro pricing) is because Hermes is silently rewriting your model name before sending it to the API.

**Check:** Look at your `agent.log` for lines like:
```
Normalized model 'deepseek-v4-flash' to 'deepseek-chat' for deepseek
```

**Our workaround:** We patched `_DEEPSEEK_CANONICAL_MODELS` in `model_normalize.py` to add `deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-v4-flash` so they pass through unchanged. See my comment on #26269 for the patch details.

Also related: #26269 (TUI still shows `deepseek-chat` which the API no longer accepts).

cases.title: Unable to add custom tools
cases.question:
I created a custom tools in tool/tool_name.py
and added in toolset.py then too I am not able to access that tool.

It's like not able to create custom tools for my self.

I followed 
https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/adding-tools

It's not working anyone facing same issue...?
cases.answer:
Automated hermes-sweeper review: current `main` already has the custom-tool surfaces this asks for.

Evidence:

- Personal/custom tools are documented as plugins now, not core edits: `website/docs/developer-guide/adding-tools.md:11` points custom/project-local tools to the plugin route, and `website/docs/guides/build-a-hermes-plugin.md:252` shows `ctx.register_tool(...)` registering tools the model can see.
- Built-in/core tool development is also wired on main: `website/docs/developer-guide/adding-tools.md:29` documents the supported files as `tools/your_tool.py` and `toolsets.py`; `tools/registry.py:57` auto-discovers top-level `registry.register(...)` calls in `tools/*.py`; `model_tools.py:180` runs that discovery at startup.
- Tool visibility still requires toolset exposure: `model_tools.py:281` states all tools must be part of a toolset to be accessible.
- Plugin loading has explicit discovery/enablement support: user plugins are scanned from `~/.hermes/plugins` in `hermes_cli/plugins.py:1192`, and standalone/user plugins are opt-in via `plugins.enabled` with a clear `hermes plugins enable ...` message at `hermes_cli/plugins.py:1282`.

The issue text mentions `tool/tool_name.py` and `toolset.py`, but the supported built-in paths are `tools/...` and `toolsets.py`; for personal tools, the supported route is a plugin enabled via `hermes plugins enable <name>`.

cases.answer:
This is not a hermes-agent bug — it's how Anthropic routes billing for third-party API access. When you use a Claude API key (as opposed to OAuth), Anthropic bills it as API usage regardless of your Pro/Max subscription. 

Related: #29125 (same class — Claude CLI + Pro/Max billing expectations), #15080 (OAuth + Max → HTTP 400 out of extra usage).

To use your Pro/Max subscription allowance through hermes-agent, you need to authenticate via OAuth (not an API key). See the docs updated in #17399 / #17404 for details on how OAuth routes through your subscription.

cases.title: How can two different Hermes isolate their files?
cases.question:
How can two different Hermes isolate their files?
If I use docker as the command running environment and enterprise wechat asks him to send files, he will not really send them successfully.
But if you use local as the command line, their files will be shared with each other again.
cases.answer:
**Two supported ways to run multiple, fully-isolated Hermes agents:**

**1. Built-in profiles (recommended)**

Hermes has first-class multi-agent support via *profiles* — each profile is a separate namespace (its own `config.yaml`, `SOUL.md`, sessions, memories, skills, credentials) under `profiles/<name>/`, with no file sharing between them.

```sh
hermes profile create work
hermes profile create personal
hermes profile list
hermes profile use work          # set a sticky default
hermes --profile personal chat   # or select per-invocation
```

You can also select a profile via the `HERMES_PROFILE` environment variable (e.g. `HERMES_PROFILE=personal hermes ...`), which is handy for gateways/containers. Each profile can run its own supervised gateway, so two agents on different platforms stay completely separate.

**2. Separate `HERMES_HOME` directories**

If you'd rather keep them in entirely distinct trees (e.g. different volumes/containers), point each agent at its own home dir with the `HERMES_HOME` env var:

```sh
HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes-work     hermes gateway run
HERMES_HOME=~/.hermes-personal hermes gateway run
```

Everything (config, keys, sessions, skills, memory) lives under that directory, so the two installs share nothing. In Docker, just mount a different host dir to `/opt/data` per container.

---

On the file-sharing behaviour you saw: with `terminal.backend: local`, tool subprocesses run in your shared host filesystem, so two agents *can* see each other's files; isolating via profiles or distinct `HERMES_HOME` dirs (and/or the Docker terminal backend) is the right fix. The broader profile-isolation hardening is tracked in #30585.

Closing as answered — please reopen if profiles/`HERMES_HOME` don't cover your setup.

cases.title: [Discussion] Why was smart_model_routing removed? Request to restore
cases.question:
## Background

The `smart_model_routing` feature was added in March 2026 (commit 4b0056159) and removed a month later in April (commit 424e9f36b, PR #12732).

This feature auto-routed short/simple turns (≤160 chars or ≤28 words) to a cheaper model, saving costs for trivial queries like "hello", "thanks", etc.

## Question

The commit message says it was "opt-in and disabled by default" but doesn't explain why it was removed wholesale instead of keeping it as an opt-in feature.

**Could you share the reasoning behind this decision?**

## User Impact

Many users find this feature useful for cost optimization:
- Simple greetings/acknowledgments don't need expensive models
- Config was `smart_model_routing.enabled: true` with `cheap_model: opencode-zen/deepseek-v4-flash-free`
- Saved tokens for trivial turns while keeping strong model for real work

## Request

1. If there were technical issues, could they be fixed instead of removing?
2. If there's a better alternative, please document it
3. Consider restoring this feature as opt-in (or with improved routing logic)

## Current Workaround

Users can manually switch models:
```bash
hermes chat -m opencode-zen/deepseek-v4-flash-free
```

But this requires manual intervention for every turn, which defeats the automation purpose.

---

cc @teknium1 (author of both the original feature and the removal)
cases.answer:
Thanks for documenting the prior implementation and the cost-saving use case.

This is an automated hermes-sweeper review. The request is being closed under the standing model-routing policy:

- Hermes does not accept complexity-based automatic model routing, cheap-vs-strong model tiers, or per-turn/per-task provider-model overrides.
- The requested restoration of `smart_model_routing` is exactly that policy category. The prior implementation was deliberately removed in 424e9f36b, and current CLI and gateway route resolution explicitly retain the session's primary model/provider.
- The linked discussion is part of the same routing cluster; related issue #20249 was closed under this policy with the same scope.
- The supported configuration point for subagents remains `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` in `config.yaml`. Manual `/model` selection and focused fixes to existing switching or fallback behavior remain separate, valid topics.

---
*Closed as not planned per standing maintainer policy (`delegation-model-routing`). This is a design-direction decision, not a judgment on the usefulness of the use case or discussion.*

---
*Closed as not-planned per standing maintainer policy (`delegation-model-routing`). This is a design-direction decision, not a code-quality judgment — see the Contribution Rubric in `AGENTS.md` for what the project is looking for. If you believe this policy was misapplied to your change, comment here and a maintainer will take a look.*

     - Restarted the gateway using:

       - systemctl --user stop/start

     gateway run)
     - Verified gateway_state.json showed Telegram as connected
     - Checked and cleared old network errors in logs
     Web UI Password Fixes Attempted

     - Set HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD=letmein (and other values) in
     /home/kelly/hermes-webui/.env
     - Deleted password/state files:

       - .signing_key

     - Ran hermes debug share and uploaded logs
     - Confirmed Python 3.14.4 and Hermes v0.14.0
cases.answer:
Hi Kelly — both issues come down to using the wrong config key / wrong component. Here's the breakdown.

## Problem 1: Telegram "Unauthorized user"

`allowed_chats` is **not** the user-authorization key — that's why it had no effect. It's a *group-chat response whitelist* (when set, the bot only responds in those group chat IDs). It does not authorize a DM user.

User authorization is checked by `_is_user_authorized()`, which looks at (in order):
1. Per-platform allow-all flag — `TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`
2. Per-platform allowlist — `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` (config key `allow_from`)
3. DM pairing-approved list
4. Global allow-all — `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`
5. Default: deny

`guest_mode: true` also won't help here — it only permits **group** messages that explicitly @mention the bot; it does nothing for DMs.

### Fix — pick one

**Option A — allowlist your user ID (recommended):**
```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
telegram:
  allow_from: "6614365140"     # comma-separated for multiple users
```
(Internally this sets `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`.)

**Option B — pairing flow:** DM the bot, it replies with a pairing code, then on the host run:
```
hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>
```

**Option C — allow everyone (only if you trust the bot's reachability):**
```yaml
telegram:
  allow_all: true              # sets TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS
```

Restart the gateway after editing config: `hermes gateway restart`.

## Problem 2: Web UI password prompt

The `bootstrap.py`, `~/.hermes/webui/`, `.pbkdf2_key`, and `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` you're working with are **not part of Hermes Agent** — there's no `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` env var or `webui/` password store anywhere in the codebase, which is why wiping those files and setting that env var changed nothing. That's a separate/third-party web UI.

Hermes' built-in dashboard is `hermes dashboard`, and its auth is **host-based**, not password-based:

| Bind host | Auth |
|---|---|
| loopback (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `::1`) | none |
| non-loopback bind (e.g. `0.0.0.0`) without `--insecure` | OAuth gate engages |
| non-loopback bind with `--insecure` | none (escape hatch) |

So:
- **Local only:** `hermes dashboard` (binds loopback, no auth). Reach it over WSL/Tailscale by port-forwarding loopback rather than binding `0.0.0.0`.
- **Bind publicly without the OAuth gate:** `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --insecure` — only do this on a trusted network (Tailscale tailnet counts; an open LAN does not). RFC1918/CGNAT/link-local addresses are treated as **public** by design.

If you specifically want the third-party `bootstrap.py` UI, that's outside this project — but for Hermes itself, `hermes dashboard` is the supported web frontend.

---

One clarifying question so we can confirm: where did the `bootstrap.py` web UI come from — a separate repo/script, or did you expect it to ship with Hermes? That'll tell us whether there's a docs gap to close.

cases.title: Question: preferred contribution path for an aX platform adapter?
cases.question:
Hi Hermes maintainers — before preparing an upstream PR, we wanted to ask whether this is an option you would be open to, and what contribution path would be most useful for this repo.

We think aX may make sense alongside Hermes because Hermes already has a platform-adapter architecture for long-running agents, and aX is an agent-native collaboration/activity layer for addressability, presence/status, spaces, mention wake/routing, durable task/context continuity, and MCP-backed capabilities.

The contribution we are imagining is intentionally small: a thin platform adapter for message delivery, presence/status, mention wake/routing, threading, and recovery. Richer capabilities would stay outside the adapter via MCP, so the adapter would not introduce a second tool stack.

We have kept the prototype/proof small and scoped, and can share a branch or patch once the preferred route is clear. We want to avoid guessing at Hermes conventions.

Would you prefer one of these paths?

1. Small platform-adapter/plugin PR
2. Example integration
3. Docs/demo recipe
4. Initial design/protocol/security issue
5. Another venue or route, such as Discord or a maintainer-preferred channel

Any adapter conventions, packaging expectations, security boundaries, or review criteria we should follow before preparing the contribution would be very helpful.

Thanks.
cases.answer:
Thanks for checking the contribution path before preparing a PR. This automated hermes-sweeper review found that current main already documents the recommended path for this exact kind of community platform adapter.

- The recommended route is a standalone platform plugin in `~/.hermes/plugins/`, rather than a core integration: `website/docs/developer-guide/adding-platform-adapters.md:9-13,31-39`.
- The guide covers the adapter contract, `ctx.register_platform()` registration, configuration and authorization hooks, multi-profile token locks, and reference implementations: `website/docs/developer-guide/adding-platform-adapters.md:21-29,117-147,174-199,455-457`.
- The guide was introduced in commit `289d2745afd2dc9ae881d0b873371bfb0eb7b228` (`docs: add platform adapter developer guide + WeCom Callback docs`).

Please use that plugin path and its referenced IRC/Teams/Google Chat/LINE examples when preparing the adapter; richer capabilities can remain outside the adapter as described in the issue.

cases.title: Guidance request: user-owned, portable LLM memory across models/tools
cases.question:
This is not necessarily a bug report; it is a request for guidance/design direction around long-term memory architecture in Hermes.

I have been dealing with this problem for several years, and I still have not found a reliable way to solve it. The problem is that I want the memory of the LLM I talk to to be under my own control.

I talked to ChatGPT for several years, and it developed a relatively good understanding of me, but the quality of its models was weak at that time. Then Google released a better model, so I moved to Gemini on the web, and from the beginning I explained myself to it again: all the things that matter to me, my concerns, my projects, and my goals. It again developed a good understanding of me. Then Anthropic released a better model, and I moved there, and the same thing happened again.

Now I am using my own server so that I can use different models, have a shared tool, and switch between models whenever I want. But now this tool itself has become another challenge.

When I find a tool better and more effective than Hermes, I will have to manually move the memory to the new tool, if it supports it and if the migration process does not have problems, because Hermes puts different things in different places: `soul.md`, `memory.md`, `user.md`, and almost every task or project generally has its own dedicated skill.

On the other hand, Hermes keeps updating `memory.md` and changes things that I manually entered myself. Over time, to make room for new things that I want it to remember, it compresses the memory more and more, which causes the quality of previous memories to be lost, because this file has a character limit.

Honestly, I do not know what the best approach is.

An LLM wiki could be one way to put related information next to each other, but I still think that an effective memory should be a semantic database built on top of an LLM wiki. The main memory should be a database, and the wiki should be the reliable documents that add details to the memory.

For example, I may remember my national ID card number, but I may not remember the other information on my national ID card. When needed, I go and pick up the national ID card, look at it, and read the details from it.

LLM memory should have the same kind of structure. When you ask an LLM something, it should know what you are talking about, and without filling the context with useless data, it should go and find only the relevant data from the correct place, and fill the context that will be sent to the LLM only with that content.

What I would like guidance on:

1. Is there a recommended architecture in Hermes for making long-term memory user-owned, portable, and model/tool agnostic?
2. Should `USER.md` / `MEMORY.md` be treated only as short bootstrap hints and pointers, while detailed memory lives in user-owned documents or a semantic store?
3. Is there a supported way to prevent Hermes from rewriting or compressing manually curated memory entries?
4. Are there existing extension points for building a semantic/vector/graph memory layer over user-owned wiki-style documents, with provenance and retrieval into context only when relevant?
5. If this is not currently supported, what would be the cleanest path to experiment with it: a custom memory provider, a plugin, Mem0/Honcho integration, skills, or some other architecture?

I am looking for guidance on the intended direction rather than asking for an immediate implementation.
cases.answer:
Thanks for the detailed architecture question. Current main now provides the requested guidance and extension path; this is an automated hermes-sweeper review.

- `website/docs/user-guide/features/memory.md:20-29` documents bounded bootstrap memory, frozen session-start injection, and non-silent overflow behavior; `:221-246` documents `memory.write_approval` to stage all memory writes for review.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/memory-providers.md:28-39` documents provider-side relevant-context prefetch, turn sync, and additive operation alongside built-in memory. It also documents self-hosted/OSS Mem0 (`:318-379`) and local SQLite Holographic memory (`:443-468`).
- Custom user-owned backends are supported through the `MemoryProvider` extension contract (`website/docs/developer-guide/memory-provider-plugin.md:26-84`) and runtime discovery from `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/` (`plugins/memory/__init__.py:109-139`).
- The underlying provider architecture landed in `924bc67eee35cc2fbb24d7cbc5649c820beb4406`.

For a portable experiment, use a local/self-hosted provider or implement a user-installed `MemoryProvider`; keep `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` as the small always-in-context tier and enable `memory.write_approval: true` for curated writes.

cases.title: When calling /v1/chat/completions, Is it possible to generate Honcho peers based on the logged-in user?
cases.question: My Hermes instance is integrated with Honcho for memory isolation. When calling /v1/chat/completions, I want to pass the currently logged-in user to Honcho so that Honcho can generate peers based on this user. Is this achievable at present?
cases.answer:
This is already supported on current `main` via the API server's stable memory-scope header. This automated hermes-sweeper review verified the implementation and its regression coverage.

- Commit `fe8560fc1249b4a7e448b5c3b80a7d213df9d78f` added `X-Hermes-Session-Key` for API-server long-term memory scoping; it is contained in release `v2026.5.7`.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:2162` parses that header on `/v1/chat/completions` and forwards it as `gateway_session_key`.
- `plugins/memory/honcho/client.py:698` uses the supplied key as the stable Honcho session scope.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/api-server.md:379` documents the intended multi-user pattern, including a user-specific key such as `agent:main:webui:dm:user-42`.

Have the authenticated frontend derive a stable key from its logged-in user and send it in `X-Hermes-Session-Key` with the API-server bearer credential.
